assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling gave chemists a general, predictable way to form aryl amines, which are ubiquitous in pharmaceuticals and materials. It is an enabling method used by a whole community, with clear mechanistic understanding of ligand effects, in the same spirit as methods that let others make what they could not before.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled catalytic systems that made the reaction general; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work was foundational but less decisive for scope. A two-person prize is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: More than three decades of independent confirmation and routine industrial use; recognition is, if anything, overdue, though the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members feel the area is already covered.
uncertainties: Whether the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize is judged to have already honored this theme.
Fair weight of Kosugi's and Migita's early contributions, from my own recollection and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors convert single bases in genomic DNA without double-strand breaks by pairing deaminase chemistry with a programmable protein. This is rationally designed molecular engineering with a direct therapeutic path, already in the clinic.
assessment.attribution: Liu's lab conceived and led the work; Komor and Gaudelli carried out the key experiments as trainees. A prize naming Liu alone, or with a CRISPR recognition elsewhere, keeps attribution clean. Note that prime editing is a separate candidate with Liu again.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade old, with growing independent clinical validation, but long-term safety and efficacy data are still accumulating; timing is slightly early but plausible.
uncertainties: Overlap with the CRISPR prize already given and with the separate prime editing candidate.
Whether the committee wants to credit trainees; clinical durability is not yet fully established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation turns a small molecule into a bridge that recruits E3 ligases to a chosen protein, a new pharmacological concept now spreading across drug discovery. The thalidomide-cereblon mechanism links molecular glues to the same principle, and structures of ternary complexes support the story.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established PROTACs as a concept and platform; Handa's lab identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. Ciulli, Gray, Ito and others also made important contributions, so credit is crowded and a three-person split excludes some strong contributors.
assessment.maturity: Clinical degraders are in late-stage trials, but approval and long-term impact are not yet complete, so recognition may be a little premature.
uncertainties: Crowded credit across PROTACs and molecular glues.
Lack of an approved PROTAC drug at the time of my knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography lets one obtain structures from micro- and nanocrystals with diffraction-before-destruction at XFELs, and time-resolved structural movies of reactions. As someone working on structure determination from tiny crystals, I value that it extends structure solution to samples that standard crystallography cannot handle.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the first SFX demonstration, Hajdu proposed and championed the diffraction-before-destruction concept, and Fromme drove the biological sample application. Schlichting is also strongly credited, so one of four deserving names is omitted, which is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of confirmation, with several facilities and many structural results; the method is mature, though its influence is concentrated among a limited number of XFEL facilities.
uncertainties: Inclusion or exclusion of Schlichting and others.
Whether this counts as chemistry rather than physics or biology; reach is limited by facility access.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes are a large new family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides made by selectively etching MAX phases, with tunable composition, conductivity and surface chemistry. Their structure-property design space, from energy storage to electromagnetic shielding, is exactly the type of materials chemistry that interests me.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum jointly reported Ti3C2 in 2011 and developed the field, which supports a natural three-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: A little over fifteen years old, with very broad independent adoption, but practical applications are still emerging and the committee may consider it somewhat early.
uncertainties: Structural control of surface terminations remains hard to verify and not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular sieves with controlled pores and active sites, including organic structure-directing agents and new frameworks, underlies refining, petrochemistry and emission control. It is an area I know well, and structure explains function directly, shown by solved framework structures.
assessment.attribution: Corma, Davis and Zones represent distinct complementary advances in catalytic design, synthesis and SDA strategy, though the field is broad and many other contributors, including Yu and Tsapatsis, are credited.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and industrial use; recognition is timely, but the prize theme is diffuse and my own research field creates a potential conflict of interest I would flag.
uncertainties: Diffuse discovery boundary and crowded credit.
Possible bias because this is my own field, so I should weigh it carefully.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers delivered an unprecedented rise in solar cell efficiency in a few years, and the materials chemistry of defect tolerance and composition tuning is intellectually rich. Impact on solar energy research is very large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first used perovskites in a solar cell, Park and Snaith drove the solid-state efficiency step change; Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also contributed, so allocation of credit is disputed.
assessment.maturity: Fast progress with wide confirmation, but stability, lead toxicity and commercialization are not resolved, so timing is arguably premature.
uncertainties: Contested credit among five or more people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-field dynamic nuclear polarization increases NMR sensitivity by orders of magnitude, enabling structural studies of surfaces, materials, and membrane proteins, a clear enabling method that extends what spectroscopy can see.
assessment.attribution: Griffin pioneered high-field DNP instrumentation and polarizing agents; Emsley developed DNP-enhanced surface and materials NMR. Bodenhausen and Prisner also contributed and could make a different configuration.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted for about two decades with commercial instruments; the method is established, but the core discovery boundaries are somewhat diffuse.
uncertainties: Relative standing against better-known magnetic resonance prizes already awarded.
